why: Both moved essentially the same traffic and were honest about what stayed, but B's system-level judgment is the one a CTO can act on: it priced the stages from real prompts, found that aider's two coding loops dominate the bill, and built the --coder-model change that actually gets that stage onto Router (A identified the same dominant stage and left it as a proposal), then reached the full Router surface — Switchyard, shadow models as the measurement that settles the model choice, a spend cap, porting the Claude path to /v1/responses to unlock Router-only fields, retuning the review loop against the ICLR benchmark the repo already ships — and ruled levers out with measurements (provider_timeout 504s without falling back, service_tier+models 400s, Flex already on). A's judgment is narrower (caching, labels, ensemble, fallbacks) and its headline model modernization is mechanism-only, but A caught two real production bugs B's tree still carries.
A_best: Finding and fixing defects that would bite in production on the models the migration itself maps onto: the ThinkingBlock crash on content[0].text across the whole modern Claude line, and the np.mean([]) nan that threw away a finished paper after a full GPU run — both surfaced live, not inferred, and B's tree still has the first one.
B_best: Ranking by measured spend and then acting on the top of that ranking: identifying aider's LiteLLM coding loops as most of a run's tokens, proving LiteLLM's Anthropic handler bypasses the runtime, and shipping --coder-model (verified end-to-end through aider on gpt-5.6-luna and switchyard) so the dominant stage can actually reach Router from a Claude run.
A_worst: It names aider as the pipeline's largest consumer and then leaves the fix as proposal i6, so under the shipped default --model claude-3-5-sonnet the biggest spend stays off Router; the visible proposal set also never reaches Switchyard, shadow models or spend caps, and its Flex analysis concludes 'inert' rather than pursuing the model move that would make it pay.
B_worst: It carries A's unfixed correctness bug: after mapping the default onto claude-sonnet-4-6, response.content[0].text can hit a ThinkingBlock and crash a multi-hour unattended run intermittently — and its s1 claim that the n=5 ensemble stays on the provider sits oddly against a validation file listing llm.py:96 as verified routing.
